narrative: Material PL1__M0419476 exhibits moderate, near-continuous daily demand averaging 566 units/day (CV=0.37) with no statistically detectable trend over the observation window March 2025 to March 2026. Lead times are highly erratic (CV=1.62, mean=0.80 days, std=0.92 days), far exceeding the stable threshold; this variability—predominantly driven by transport uncertainty—is the primary contributor to the required safety stock of 958 units at the 95% service level. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy with reorder point 1,956 units and a storage-capacity-capped order quantity of 4,281 units reduces estimated annual inventory costs by approximately $27,423 (-89%) relative to the current SAP configuration, chiefly through order batch consolidation from ~610 to ~39 replenishments per year. Escalation to procurement for lead time SLA renegotiation is strongly recommended.
warnings: Lead time CV=1.62 exceeds stable threshold (0.6); escalation to procurement recommended for supplier SLA review.
Storage capacity constraint is binding: unconstrained EOQ=4698 capped to 4281 units to satisfy max_storage_units=5239.707 with safety_stock=958.
Safety stock increase of +193% required versus current SAP value of 327 units; ERP update needed immediately.
Recommended safety lead time (2.01 days) is lower than current SAP setting (3.0 days); reduction will improve ordering efficiency.

research_insights.selection_rationale: With a non-zero demand fraction of 100% and a moderate CV of 0.37, demand is sufficiently regular to support a continuous-review policy. The (r,Q) model minimises total ordering and holding costs via the EOQ formula while the reorder point absorbs lead time and demand variability through an analytically derived safety stock. This is preferable to a periodic-review model given the high lead time instability, as it triggers replenishment immediately when stock falls to the reorder point rather than waiting for the next review cycle.
research_insights.boundary_risk: The storage cap (max_storage_units=5239.707) binds and reduces the order quantity from the unconstrained EOQ of 4,698 to 4,281 units. This increases order frequency slightly (from ~30 to ~39 orders/year) and raises annual ordering cost by approximately $450, but the policy remains capacity-feasible. If demand grows or safety stock must be increased further, the storage constraint will become more restrictive and may require a warehouse capacity review.
research_insights.escalation_flag: Lead time CV=1.62 is classified as highly unstable and requires immediate escalation to procurement. The current 58 lead time observations range from 0.04 to 4.46 working days, suggesting inconsistent supplier or transport performance. Negotiating tighter lead time SLAs or identifying a secondary supplier would significantly reduce required safety stock and improve service level reliability.
